citations.review_text:
Metro 2033 was already a 10/10 for me, this one adds more of what i like in these types of games. I love how we can choose to play stealth or just rampage in a lot of missions. The lore goes deeper and sets the story for exodus, excited to play that one.

One small complain i have is the compass. It points to where the objective is but not how to get there. It's not too difficult to figure it out but i wished it lead you the entire way

**Recommended, especially if you already played Metro 2033.**

Metro: Last Light Redux is basically Metro 2033, but better in almost every way. The combat feels better, the environments are more varied, the pacing is stronger, and the game generally does a much better job of turning the Metro universe into an actual adventure rather than just a sequence of grim tunnels.

One of the biggest improvements is that **most of my frustrations with Metro 2033 are simply gone here**. In the first game, I regularly struggled to figure out where the game wanted me to go, whether something was scripted, whether an NPC had glitched, or whether I was missing some poorly marked exit. Last Light felt much clearer and smoother. I could spend my time actually playing the game instead of occasionally fighting the level design.

The biggest caveat is that I would **absolutely not recommend starting here**. Last Light assumes you understand Artyom, the Dark Ones, D6, the Rangers, and the basic political landscape of the Metro. Even having played 2033 recently, I occasionally had to remind myself who people were and what exactly the Red Line was trying to accomplish. Without the first game's context, I think a lot of the emotional weight of Artyom realizing what he did to the Dark Ones would be completely lost.

Like the first game, the atmosphere is still the star. The stations feel lived-in, the surface is miserable and dangerous, and there is constantly a sense that you're moving through a much larger world than the relatively short campaign actually shows you. The story also gets much more interesting once the young Dark One joins Artyom and the game starts connecting his guilt over the first game's ending with the political struggle over D6.

There are still a few weaker sections. The railcar and swamp areas dragged a bit for me, especially when optional side paths seemed to offer very little of interest. But those moments never became the kind of friction I felt in Metro …

citations.review_text:
I’ve now 100% completed Metro: Last Light Redux on PlayStation, Xbox, and Steam, and out of the first two Metro games, this one is still my favorite.

The story continues from the canon ending of Metro 2033, where Artyom destroyed the Dark Ones, and I liked where they took it from there. The gameplay feels smoother, the levels have more variety, and it does not feel quite as claustrophobic as the first game. You still spend plenty of time underground, but there are more outdoor sections and different environments, which kept the game from feeling repetitive.

The two Redux games play very similarly, but Last Light feels more polished and improved overall.

I also played all the DLC, and my favorite parts were the short missions with Anna, Pavel, and Khan. They do not drastically change the main story, but they add some nice background to the characters and the world. They are pretty short, so I probably would have been disappointed if I had paid full price for them separately. Since Redux includes them, though, they are definitely worth playing.

I bought the Metro games together in a bundle on sale, and that is how I would recommend getting them. If you like atmospheric, story-driven single-player shooters, Metro: Last Light Redux is absolutely worth playing.

Three platforms later, it is still my favorite of the first two.

    [*]While not much in gameplay has changed, the new [spoiler]snipers[/spoiler] introduced are incredibly satisfying to play with
    [*]The [spoiler]Dark One child wearing clothes[/spoiler] is super wholesome lol

    [*]The [spoiler]Dark One child having the voice of a generic child[/spoiler] really throws me off a bit, I understand it's probs a budget thing, but still

Metro Last Light Redux - 100%

Combat: As good as the last one. Guns feel perfect for this world, and you have a great variation through the entire game. Headshots are satisfying, and both stealth or guns blazing feel like viable options.
World Building: Metro is one of my more favourite settings. Most of it being in an underground metro making things creepy, dark and very end of the world type of feeling. 
Story: Really good. The previous game was solid, but this one pushes it a bit further, with feelings of forgiving or revenge. Was fully engaged from start to finish, and had some memorable side characters.
Achievements: This one is a mix. I loved my first playthrough, having to do specific stuff in certain levels made it alot of fun to go through. Collectibles were also decently easy to find, though a decent grind. But with any game having achievements for multiple endings/difficulty, replaying games is never too fun for me. Then there's also the extra levels, some were great, some were terrible. 
All in all though, i had a solid experience, that ended on a tiny bit of a sour note with repetition and some grinding levels.

citations.review_text:
Metro: Last Light Redux is a masterclass in atmospheric, post-apocalyptic storytelling. Building on the incredible foundation of its predecessor, the game plunges you back into the hauntingly beautiful, radiation-blasted ruins of the Moscow metro system.

The Redux edition includes all previously released DLC and adds new gameplay modes, letting you choose between a tense, survival-horror experience or a more action-focused shooter. Exceptional lighting, sound design, and environmental details make every encounter with the mutated deep-dwelling horrors genuinely thrilling. For newcomers to the series, this is the definitive way to experience Artyom's journey.

Key Highlights

* Immersive Atmosphere: The game perfectly captures the dread and claustrophobia of the underground tunnels, contrasted with the lethal beauty of the irradiated surface.

* Play Your Way: With the addition of "Survival" and "Spartan" modes, you can choose between a scarce, methodical survival experience or a more combat-heavy, resource-rich approach.

* The Definitive Package: It includes all the original DLC, adding hours of extra content and different perspectives on the Metro universe.

I’ve now 100% completed Metro: Last Light Redux on PlayStation, Xbox, and Steam, and out of the first two Metro games, this one is still my favorite.

The story continues from the canon ending of Metro 2033, where Artyom destroyed the Dark Ones, and I liked where they took it from there. The gameplay feels smoother, the levels have more variety, and it does not feel quite as claustrophobic as the first game. You still spend plenty of time underground, but there are more outdoor sections and different environments, which kept the game from feeling repetitive.

The two Redux games play very similarly, but Last Light feels more polished and improved overall.

I also played all the DLC, and my favorite parts were the short missions with Anna, Pavel, and Khan. They do not drastically change the main story, but they add some nice background to the characters and the world. They are pretty short, so I probably would have been disappointed if I had paid full price for them separately. Since Redux includes them, though, they are definitely worth playing.

I bought the Metro games together in a bundle on sale, and that is how I would recommend getting them. If you like atmospheric, story-driven single-player shooters, Metro: Last Light Redux is absolutely worth playing.

Three platforms later, it is still my favorite of the first two.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the narrative as a direct continuation of the first game's story, focusing on redemption and factions in the metro.

citations.review_text:
"The hellfire I created with my own hands using D6's missiles was not enough to illuminate the darkness within my soul; now, a single ray of hope, born from the ashes, awaits me so that I may pay the price for my sins."

Metro: Last Light, the claustrophobic dread of our underground existence is magnified by the crushing weight of my own guilt after annihilating the Dark Ones. This chapter of my journey transcends mere survival; it is a desperate quest for redemption as the Metro's factions—blinded by greed and twisted ideologies—march toward a devastating war over the D6 bunker. Guided by the last surviving Little Dark One, I have come to realize that the terrifying mutants and the suffocating radiation of the surface are secondary to the monstrous ambitions of my fellow men. Balancing tense stealth, brutal firefights, and the relentless scarcity of our ruined world, this profound psychological odyssey proves that even in our darkest tunnels, a single spark of forgiveness might be enough to light the way forward, making it a haunting 10/10 masterpiece on the endurance of the human spirit.

Sequels often downgraded from their predecessor, but not with Metro series. The story is deeper and longer; it's about redeeming yourself (player or Artyom) after what he did in the first game (canon bad ending). Unlike the previous game, you have to work harder to gain canon good ending in this sequel.

I like the irony in this game: "If it's hostile you kill it". Turns out it isn't hostile but you killed it already...

After finishing Metro 2033 Redux, I couldn't wait to continue Artyom's story in Metro: Last Light Redux. I also read Dmitry Glukhovsky's Metro novels, so experiencing the games after reading the books made the world feel even more immersive.

What I love most about this series is the atmosphere. The Metro is dark, mysterious, and constantly keeps you on edge. Every station has its own personality, and even after many hours I still found myself slowing down just to take in the environment and listen to the conversations around me.

Last Light improves almost everything from Metro 2033. The gunplay feels better, stealth is more enjoyable, weapon customization adds more depth, and the story does a great job expanding the world without losing the feeling of isolation and survival.

I also appreciate that the game doesn't rely only on action. Some of my favorite moments were simply exploring the tunnels, discovering small details, and seeing how people try to survive in such a harsh world.

Even today, the Redux version looks fantastic. The lighting, sound design, and overall atmosphere still compete with many modern games.

Now I've completed both Metro 2033 Redux and Metro: Last Light Redux, and I can honestly say this has become one of my favorite game series. I can't wait to continue with Metro Exodus.

If you enjoy story-driven games with incredible world-building and atmosphere, don't skip this one. It's absolutely worth your time.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that turning up tessellation too high causes graphical issues.

citations.review_text:
Fantastic follow up to 2033. LL is much longer and gives the world more development. the stealth remains somewhat basic and at times frustrating but not enough to make you abandon that play style. the game still looks great and I'd recommend it to anyone that enjoyed the first entry. 

Putting tessellation at 16x caused graphical bugs for me, so I'd suggest leaving it at 8x. I would also avoid Alt-Tab-ing as this sometimes caused delayed crashing that would interrupt gameplay
It may have some slight issues running on modern / current gen hardware but this game is a Classic, its story holds up even to today cannot recommend it highly enough.

claims.claim: Reviewers mention that the game requires technical fixes or modifications to run properly on modern hardware.

citations.review_text: A good, if dated, euro-jank FPS game that holds up well enough for one playthrough. You come to Metro for the world but not the writing. Just a heads up: It requires some fixing to get running well such as mods to remove the unskippable intro movies and disabling anti-aliasing to get more than 30 FPS on modern hardware.
It may have some slight issues running on modern / current gen hardware but this game is a Classic, its story holds up even to today cannot recommend it highly enough.
